extracted.intended_audience: practicing photographers, photography students, and photography enthusiasts interested in documentary and landscape work
extracted.subtask_description: Explaining the aesthetic, technical, and ethical criteria that characterize Sebastião Salgado's social documentary and environmental photography, useful for photographers seeking to learn from his practice. Focuses on style (black & white, composition, light), project practice (long-term immersion), technical craft (film, printing), and advocacy/ethical stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Striking compositions and emotional depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado's images are celebrated for their emotional depth, striking compositions, and exquisite use of light and shadow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for compositions that convey emotional charge and narrative weight; use framing and tonality to emphasize the subject's dignity and the story being told. The page highlights 'striking compositions' and 'emotional depth' as core qualities of his work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black and white photography as a deliberate choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado's decision to work exclusively in black and white is a conscious choice, allowing him to create images with a timeless quality and to emphasize the emotional content of his subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monochrome to strip distractions and focus on tonality, contrast, texture, and emotion. Treat black & white as an expressive decision rather than a default; it's used to 'emphasize the emotional content' and produce a 'timeless quality.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term project commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado is known for his commitment to long-term photographic projects, often spending years immersed in the communities and environments he documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time to develop deep understanding and relationships with subjects; long immersion enables authenticity and empathy in storytelling. The page states this approach 'enables him to develop a deep understanding of his subjects and to capture their stories with authenticity and empathy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine art printing and darkroom technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado works closely with master printer Pablo Inirio to produce his photographs as silver gelatin prints, using traditional darkroom techniques to achieve exceptional tonal range and detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize printmaking and darkroom processes to realize the full tonal and textural potential of images. The emphasis on silver gelatin prints and working with a master printer indicates printing is integral to the final aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of resilience and dignity in subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: His work often portrays the resilience and dignity of marginalized and impoverished communities, with a strong focus on the human connection to the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame subjects to convey their humanity and dignity rather than exploiting suffering; focus on resilience and context. The page stresses documenting 'the dignity of work' and that photography should 'make [a human] noble.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Human–environment connection as a thematic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A recurring theme is the human connection to the environment—documenting how communities and landscapes interact, and the effects of environmental change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat landscape and environment not just as backdrop but as active elements in human stories; projects like 'Genesis' exemplify long-term engagement with pristine environments to raise awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical stance: photography as advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado combines documentary practice with environmental and humanitarian advocacy, e.g., founding Instituto Terra and producing projects that raise awareness about environmental degradation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photography to inform and advocate responsibly; consider follow-up actions (institutions, exhibitions, books) that translate images into conservation or social initiatives. The page links his photographic work with concrete advocacy (Instituto Terra, Genesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and material choices to support aesthetic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout his career Salgado has used 35mm film cameras (Leica M6, Canon EOS-1V), medium format (Pentax 67, Mamiya 7), prime lenses (Leica Summicron-M 35mm f/2, Summilux-M 50mm f/1.4), and Kodak Tri-X 400 black and white film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose cameras, formats, lenses, and film that support the tonal, textural, and compositional goals of the project; film and medium-format choices are part of achieving Salgado's characteristic look and tonality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative and publication as part of project completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Major projects culminate in books, exhibitions, and films (e.g., Workers, Genesis, The Salt of the Earth), which form part of the practice and dissemination of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan projects with an end-form in mind (book, exhibition, film) so the body of work can have wider impact and reach; publication and exhibition are integral to transforming documentary work into advocacy and legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making subjects 'noble'—a moral guideline for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted principle: 'If you take a picture of a human that does not make him noble, there is no reason to take this picture. That is my way of seeing things.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a representational ethic that seeks to ennoble rather than sensationalize subjects; prioritize respect and humanity in framing, captioning, and dissemination.
